correctness.summary: The published 14-system KTS file was decoded independently from its 21-by-10 symbol format. Each decoded object has 70 triples and covers all 210 unordered point pairs exactly once. A fresh brute force six-set Pasch counter gives zero for all 14 systems. A separate root/leg transversal mitre counter gives the vector [45,51,39,39,27,42,45,35,21,21,42,44,46,45], so the exact minimum is 21 and is attained by systems 8 and 9. This reproduces the record without relying on its stored raw count file or its Python counters.

limitations: Completeness of the 14-system universe is taken from the published Kokkala-Östergård classification/dataset; the 83,003,869 anti-Pasch STS(21) were not re-enumerated.
The independent audit recomputed the combinatorial counts from the archived 14-system data, not from the original 6.1 GB anti-Pasch STS(21) corpus.
The result is a finite computational census rather than a structural proof of a general lower bound.
No priority claim is made for the count vector.

originality.summary: Kokkala and Östergård already supply the complete set of 14 anti-Pasch KTS(21) isomorphism classes. The audited contribution is the exact mitre-count statistic over that published finite dataset, not the classification itself. The audit found no evidence that the count vector is a previously stated theorem, but makes no priority claim from that absence.

scientific_value.summary: The result answers the finite target exactly and supplies a reproducible obstruction to 5-sparsity for every resolvable anti-Pasch STS(21) in the complete published list. Its scope is deliberately finite and dataset-relative.
